attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Faithful. The sentence has two parts: a firm claim that both companies are unprofitable, and a pricing inference hedged by 'likely'. Under policy, only the firm unprofitability part can be scored.

contract.note: The support condition requires evidence of a substantial pricing shortfall, which scores the 'likely' clause. Policy says hedged language is not scored. Only the firm unprofitability part should be judged. Choosing 2024 as the period from context is reasonable.

evidence.note: October 2024 report of OpenAI's own expected loss for 2024. It is a company projection, not a realized result, and covers only OpenAI.
Audited GAAP figures show Anthropic had a 2024 net loss, so it was unprofitable. The contract's basis is press estimates, and the filing says nothing about OpenAI or about pricing shortfalls.

reviews.rationale: The hedged pricing clause ('likely charging nowhere near enough') cannot be scored. On the firm unprofitability claim, the packet shows Anthropic's audited 2024 loss, but on a different accounting basis than the contract uses. For OpenAI it offers only a pre-year-end projection of a loss, not a realized result. The packet therefore does not establish realized unprofitability for both companies on the contract's basis.

attribution.note: Zitron restates and endorses a point he says he has made repeatedly.

semantics.note: Faithful to his claim that generative AI is a dead end because of hallucination. The aside setting aside other reasons (economics, data, value) is reasonably left out.

contract.note: Reading 'dead end' as a fundamental barrier to dependable applications is an ordinary reading of firm language. The phrase has no threshold, so the result depends on that interpretation.

evidence.note: Theoretical paper showing hallucination cannot be fully eliminated under formal assumptions. That supports the premise, not the dead-end conclusion.
A 2020-21 customer-support deployment found productivity gains with human oversight. It shows the tools were useful, but it does not measure a reliability ceiling or later progress.

reviews.rationale: The packet confirms that hallucination is inherent, which is the premise. It also shows useful human-assisted deployment. Neither item shows whether hallucination blocks, or fails to block, meaningful progress toward dependable applications, so the causal claim stays unsettled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Trapped in amber' fairly means generative AI products made no material progress for over a year. The context says stronger models 'do not unlock new features', which supports that reading.

contract.note: Testing for materially new, accessible capabilities in the year before the post is a fair, ordinary reading of firm language. It does not import the stronger 'industry-defining' standard.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own announcement: computer use was released in public beta on the API on 22 Oct 2024. This is a company disclosure, but the release is a dated, verifiable event.
Independent November 2024 case study confirms the released computer-use capability performed new end-to-end desktop actions.
Google's September 2024 launch of NotebookLM Audio Overview, a new, accessible user workflow. Company disclosure, with limitations acknowledged.

reviews.rationale: Within Dec 2023 to Dec 2024, users could access materially new capabilities: Claude computer use, independently confirmed, and NotebookLM audio discussions. Both releases were experimental, but each enabled new kinds of tasks. That contradicts the claim of product stagnation for over a year.

attribution.note: Zitron's own statement, summarising reported estimates in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'On course to lose more than $5 billion this year' is unhedged, so treating it as a scored forecast for calendar 2024 is acceptable. The strict 'more than' threshold is kept.

contract.note: Holding the outcome to the accounting basis of the estimate he relied on (which excluded equity compensation) is defensible. The speaker named no basis, though. A plain reading of GAAP net loss could yield a different result.

evidence.note: September 2024 report of OpenAI's own projected loss of about $5B, excluding equity compensation. A projection, not the outcome.
June 2026 report of an audited 2024 GAAP net loss just over $5B, with an operating loss of about $8.8B. Not reconciled to the estimate's basis, so context only.

reviews.rationale: The deadline has passed. The only realized figure is a GAAP net loss just over $5B, which is on a different basis from the estimate that excluded equity compensation. No result on the contract's basis is in the packet. On a plain GAAP reading the claim might be supported, but under the contract it stays unsettled.
